sources: https://gastateparks.reserveamerica.com/campgroundDetails.do?contractCode=GA&parkId=530194 (Services & Amenities; every site's details page incl. GIS points, 1-night price for 2027-06-15 and Sat 2026-11-14), read 2026-10-29

values.note: $40 a night at the back-in sites (electric and water); $48 at the pull-throughs, which include the 18 sewer sites ($280 / $336 a week). The same on a Saturday in November 2026 and a Tuesday in June 2027. The park sits inside the Okefenokee National Wildlife Refuge, so a $5 refuge fee is charged on top of the ParkPass, which overnight guests pay once per vehicle per stay.

fees.source: https://gastateparks.reserveamerica.com/campgroundDetails.do?contractCode=GA&parkId=530194 (30 public sites '$40.00 Per Night , $280.00 Per Week', 20 '$48.00 Per Night , $336.00 Per Week' for 2027-06-15 and 2026-11-14); https://gastateparks.org/Okefenokee ('Because Okefenokee State Park is located within a National Wildlife Refuge, gates lock at closing (10 p.m.) and a $5 refuge fee is charged'; 'Overnight guests pay daily ParkPass fee only once per vehicle during their stay'), read 2026-10-29

hookups.source: gastateparks.reserveamerica.com parkId 530194 site details (all 50 public sites 'Electricity Hookup: 50/30', 'Water Hookup: Y'; 'Sewer Hookup: Y' at public pull-throughs 29-35, 39, 41-46 and 49-52, bookable at $48), read 2026-10-29

values.note: Two loops, every site with 50/30-amp electric and water. The RV loop (29-52, 24 sites) takes a 23-ft rig at every site: 30-50 ft, 18 full-hookup pull-throughs. The other loop (2-28, 26 sites) runs 15-35 ft; only seven of its sites (2, 4, 11, 14, 15 and pull-throughs 23 and 26) take a 23-ft rig. 31 sites in all fit.

values.note: Park gates lock at 10 pm (inside the national wildlife refuge); the park is open 7 am - 10 pm.

booking.source: https://gastateparks.org/Okefenokee (reservation links -> gastateparks.reserveamerica.com ... parkId=530194; 'gates lock at closing (10 p.m.)'; 'Hours: Park 7 a.m.–10 p.m.'), read 2026-10-29

note: GA state park inside the Okefenokee National Wildlife Refuge near Fargo, a main entrance to the swamp; boat tours and canoe/kayak rentals, certified dark-sky park. Renovated campground reopened Aug 2025. Formerly Stephen C. Foster State Park (renamed 2026). --Claude
